title: Roadmap Orchestra: Q3 Execution Playbook for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a single-quarter ‘execution playbook’ that maps our Q3 roadmap commitments for the Hosted API and Model Catalog into concrete sprint-level work, canary schedules, and OKR-linked milestones. Goal is to reduce cross-team coordination overhead, provide a repeatable canary cadence for new models/endpoints, and ensure measurable guards for quality and cost.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Consolidate OKRs and initiative-level outcomes for Hosted API + Model Catalog into a prioritized sprint plan for the next 10 weeks.
- Define canary windows, rollout criteria, and automatic rollback triggers tied to quality and cost metrics.
- Establish a lightweight release choreography (roles, runbook links, dashboards) so PM/Eng/Design can execute without weekly ad-hoc meetings.
- Deliver the playbook doc, a tracked Linear epic (this ticket) with child tasks, and a dashboard template for realtime monitoring.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
1) Playbook doc published to Confluence (link below) with clear ownership for each milestone.
2) Canary schedule defined: 2% traffic (24h) -> 10% (48h) -> 50% (72h) -> 100% gated on metrics.
3) Automated checks connected to the console dashboard: latency P95 <= 450ms or rollback; token cost delta <= +12% allowed; quality regression (eval suite) < 1.5% regression rate.
4) Child Linear issues created for engineering work and canary infra; milestone dates assigned.
5) Stakeholder sync runbook and on-call rotation documented.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Strict canary size vs time-to-value: smaller initial canaries reduce risk but slow rollout; agreed to use 2% start for externally facing model changes and 5% for non-model runtime changes.
- Cost gating sensitivity: aggressive cost gates can prevent useful rollouts; agreed threshold +12% token cost as a soft gate that triggers PM review rather than automatic rollback for curated models.
- Eval coverage vs speed: extensive eval suites improve safety but lengthen pre-release pipeline. We will run a minimal fast eval on CI and a full eval in staging nightly; if full eval shows regression, initiate immediate canary pause.

Key stakeholders and owners:
- PM lead: Jordan Patel (assignee) — overall playbook owner and exec updates.
- Engineering lead: Maya Singh — runtime and canary automation.
- Model ops: Daniel Park — model profiling and regression guards.
- Design/Docs: Priya Rao — public-facing docs and onboarding flows.

Artifacts / links:
- Playbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/roadmap-orchestra-q3-hostedapi-modelcatalog (draft)
- Eval harness (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/hosted-api-evals/Q3-playbook
- Canary infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5632
- Dashboard template (Console): console.redwood.ai/dashboards/templates/roadmap-orchestra-q3

Proposed sprint milestones (high level):
- Week 1 (2026-03-16 -> 2026-03-22): Finalize priorities and create child Linear tasks; baseline metrics collection.
- Week 2: Implement canary traffic routing + lightweight gating checks.
- Week 3-4: Integrate eval harness into pre-release pipeline; create smoke tests for model variants.
- Week 5: First hosted-model canary run (internal customers) and cost/latency review.
- Week 6-8: Iterate on findings, broaden canary to selected external customers.
- Week 9-10: Stabilize rollout, bake into release cadence for subsequent quarters.

Risk register / mitigations:
- Risk: Canary detection blind spots for semantic regressions. Mitigation: maintain curated prompt set targeted per taxonomy, and require model-owner signoff for high-risk categories.
- Risk: Capacity shortages during rollouts. Mitigation: pre-reserve burst capacity in Dedicated pools and add fallback routing policy to older stable variants.
- Risk: Dashboard false positives. Mitigation: implement smoothing and require sustained violation (>=30 minutes) before automatic pause.

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Jordan P.: finalize playbook and publish to Confluence (ETA: 2026-03-15) — DONE (published draft).
- Maya S.: open infra PR for canary routing and autoscaling hooks (ETA: 2026-03-19) — IN PROGRESS (PR #5632).
- Daniel P.: assemble evaluation prompt subsets for top 6 hosted endpoints (ETA: 2026-03-20) — IN PROGRESS.
- Priya R.: update customer-facing FAQs and onboarding flows (ETA: 2026-03-25) — TODO.

Open questions for leadership: 
- Approval on cost gate behavior: do we want automatic rollback or PM review at +12%? (Recommendation: PM review for model catalog, auto-rollback for infra regressions.)
- Agree on the primary KPIs to tie to OKR (we propose: rollout velocity (time-to-100%), model-health regression %, avg token cost).

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync on Mondays for the first 6 weeks, then move to biweekly.
- Exec summary update at the end of Week 4 with canary metrics and recommended next steps.

Notes on how this differs from prior playbooks:
- Focused on orchestration across Hosted API and Model Catalog rather than model curation alone; includes explicit routing fallbacks and cost-aware gating.
- Standardized canary cadence and automated dashboard checks tied to rollback triggers.

Historical context / references: 
- Draws on runbook patterns from PM-21034 and the hosted endpoints tier playbook (PM-21034 link above).
- Incorporates lessons from the Q2 incident where a model rollout caused a 25% latency regression due to batching misconfiguration; the playbook requires a pre-rollout smoke test that mirrors production sequence lengths.
